analysis.title: GS SECTOR SPECIALISTS: Energy, Natural Resources and Utilities Preview Three Stocks 29 Oct 2026
key_insights: PBF: desk positioning score was 7/10 into the print. Reported EPS beat the Street by 15%. The main focus is the cash build and net debt inflection first highlighted at 2Q results.
PBF: total net debt fell 150% versus 2Q26 and the company holds $2.5bn of cash against an $8.6bn market cap, implying net cash of about $430mn.
Refiners: feedback is mixed on how to use cash (share repurchases vs building cash vs smaller projects). Use of cash is expected to be questions 1, 2 and 3 on the 8:30 AM call.

Refiners: the bar is high for the remaining prints, even after the group's relative underperformance versus the broader Energy complex. Specialist inbounds point to crack softness, which is a seasonal gasoline roll.

Refiners: the WCS differential is now $31/b. A PSX call quote from the prior day says weaker heavy differentials favor PSX, heavy crude is a race to the bottom for Canadian and Venezuelan supply and high-sulfur fuel oil, and Canadian crude is currently favored.

FTI: specialists have leaned negative for some time and the results largely reinforce the cautious view. Subsea orders were light for a second straight quarter at $2.05bn versus expectations nearer $2.5bn.
FTI: there is an ongoing question about market share losses to peers. FY2027 early guidance is in line with the Street on Subsea revenue, and the adj. EBITDA margin of 23% at the midpoint is on par.
FTI: the stock trades at 11.5x FY2 EBITDA. The likely call question is whether other names offer better relative value given an offshore cycle and potential for more O&G capex.
DTM: a quiet quarter was expected and delivered. Expectations were an in-line quarter, an FY guidance raise and a MIST South Phase 1 update, and all three were met.

DTM: the question is what management can say to give confidence in the next leg of growth. Order backlog gets more focus nearer year-end and the annual update. The stock has underperformed WMB and KMI by about 20% YTD, and early inbounds show no real enthusiasm.

market_movers.rationale: EPS beat the Street by 15% and net debt fell sharply with $2.5bn of cash. Use of cash is the main call topic.
Subsea orders of $2.05bn missed expectations near $2.5bn for a second quarter running. Specialists lean negative and market share loss is a live question.
The quarter was in line and the setup skewed negative on the desk. The stock trails WMB and KMI by about 20% YTD with no real enthusiasm yet.

sector_views.rationale: The bar is high for remaining prints after relative underperformance versus Energy. Cracks are seasonally soft and use-of-cash views are mixed. A wider WCS differential of $31/b is noted as favorable to heavy-crude processors.
Specialists lean negative on FTI because of light Subsea orders and share-loss concerns.
DTM delivered an in-line quarter with limited enthusiasm and trails WMB and KMI.

earnings_insights: PBF: EPS beat the Street by 15% (reported basis not specified in the note). Total net debt reduction of 150% versus 2Q26, cash of $2.5bn, market cap $8.6bn, net cash about $430mn. The desk's positioning score into the print was 7/10. Call at 8:30 AM.

FTI: Subsea orders reported at $2.05bn versus expectations near $2.5bn, light for the second quarter in a row. FY2027 early guidance is in line with the Street on Subsea revenue. Adj. EBITDA margin guidance is 23% at the midpoint, on par with the Street. The stock trades at 11.5x FY2 EBITDA.

DTM: the quarter was in line with expectations, FY guidance was raised and a MIST South Phase 1 update was given, all as expected. Order backlog will get more focus closer to year-end and the annual update.
PSX (read-across): on its call the prior day, PSX said weaker heavy crude differentials play into its system and that it imports more Canadian crude into the US than any other company.

macro_indicators.interpretation: A wide Western Canadian Select discount to benchmark crude benefits refiners able to run heavy crude.

risk_factors: Refiners: crack spread softness, with the seasonal roll in gasoline.
Refiners: a high bar for the remaining earnings prints.
FTI: continued light Subsea orders and possible market share losses to peers.
DTM: lack of visible growth catalysts and an order backlog update not due until closer to year-end.
